title: Why the Allianz Arena will be illuminated in orange on Wednesday
summary: As in previous years, Bayern Munich are marking the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women and showing their support for the “Zonta Says No” initiative by illuminating the Allianz Arena
content:
As in previous years, Bayern Munich are marking the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women and showing their support for the “Zonta Says No” initiative by illuminating the Allianz Arena in orange on Wednesday, November 25.

This year, Zonta is focusing on digital violence, from threats and cyberstalking to sexually explicit images generated and shared using AI.

“Behind threats, cyberstalking and the distribution of sexually explicit images are real people – and these actions have real consequences," said FC Bayern president Herbert Hainer.

"As FC Bayern, we do not want to turn a blind eye.

Instead, we want to take a stand and help empower those affected.

title: Werder make stance clear on Niclas Füllkrug ahead of January window amid Bayern links
summary: Topping the Bundesliga scoring charts with 10 goals, Niclas Füllkrug has been a big hit since returning to Werder Bremen on loan from West Ham United last summer. The 33-year-old's impressive form has led to sp
content:
Topping the Bundesliga scoring charts with 10 goals, Niclas Füllkrug has been a big hit since returning to Werder Bremen on loan from West Ham United last summer.

The 33-year-old's impressive form has led to speculation that his loan spell could be cut short in January to allow him to join an even bigger club, with Bayern Munich, for example, reportedly considering signing a new striker following Harry Kane's long-term injury.

Unsurprisingly, however, Werder Bremen are reluctant to let their top scorer leave when the winter transfer window opens.

“Niclas leaving in the winter is not up for discussion for us,” Werder Bremen head of first team football Peter Niemeyer told DeichStube.

Werder have already made it clear that they would like to sign Füllkrug on a permanent basis at the end of the season, but whether they will be able to do so depends on West Ham and the financial terms of a potential deal.

content:
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Rayan Cherki (left) rescued a late draw for Manchester City against Napoli Manchester City reporter at Etihad StadiumPublished44 minutes agoManchester City's slick footballing machine is starting to grind to a halt.

The quick passing patterns and edge-of-the-seat action that was evident for so long under former manager Pep Guardiola was supposed to be taken forward by incumbent Enzo Maresca.

It started flawlessly under the Italian with the side winning their first eight games, but that smooth operation is beginning to turn into a turgid and pedestrian showing.

Similar to Saturday's 1-1 draw against Fulham, moans and groans filled a rather flat Etihad Stadium as the home faithful watched their side labour to a 2-2 Champions League draw against Napoli.

City's recent defensive issues also continued, now conceding in 10 successive games and letting in the first goal in seven of those matches.

content:

Arsenal reporter at Emirates StadiumPublished17 minutes agoIt might be emerging more as a theme than as a major problem, but in recent weeks Arsenal cannot seem to finish off matches when they are on top.

In their past nine outings across all competitions, just once have the Gunners won a game by more than a single goal.

The latest frustration came in Tuesday's 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund, though perspective is needed.

Arsenal might consider it as two points dropped having gone into half-time ahead, but they remain unbeaten in the current Champions League league phase and have not lost at this stage of the competition for more than two years.

content:
Borussia Dortmund striker Serhou Guirassy believes he belongs among the world's top five forwards and has not ruled out winning the Ballon d'Or.

In an interview with “Bild”, the 30-year-old also opened up about his relationship with Fábio Silva and his future at the Bundesliga club.

Asked whether he receives enough recognition, Guirassy made a confident assessment of his position in world football.

"If you look at the last three or four years, there are strikers like Kane and Mbappé – and I would say that I might be fourth or fifth," he explained.

summary: The Bundesliga could introduce a new Saturday evening kick-off time from the 2029/30 season as part of the next domestic television rights cycle. According to Bild, plans are being drawn up to stage five marque
content:
The Bundesliga could introduce a new Saturday evening kick-off time from the 2029/30 season as part of the next domestic television rights cycle.

According to Bild, plans are being drawn up to stage five marquee Bundesliga fixtures per season at 20:30 CET on Saturday evenings.

The proposal was reportedly well received at a meeting of the 36 Bundesliga and 2.

Bundesliga clubs in Frankfurt at the beginning of October, with the prospect of attracting larger television audiences in a prime-time slot appealing to potential broadcasters.

Crucially, the traditional Saturday 15:30 kick-off time would remain unaffected, as would the existing 18:30 slot.

title: Lazio ultras temporarily lift Stadio Olimpico boycott but not everybody agrees
summary: ROME, ITALY - AUGUST 16: SS Lazio and Mantova 1911 remembered Livio Berruti with a minute's silence prior the Coppa Italia match between SS Lazio and Mantova 1911 at Stadio Olimpico on August 16, 2026 in Rome,
content:
ROME, ITALY - AUGUST 16: SS Lazio and Mantova 1911 remembered Livio Berruti with a minute's silence prior the Coppa Italia match between SS Lazio and Mantova 1911 at Stadio Olimpico on August 16, 2026 in Rome, Italy.

(Photo by Marco Rosi - SS Lazio/Getty Images) Ultras of Lazio’s Curva Nord have announced that they will temporarily lift their Stadio Olimpico boycott for their Serie A clash at home against Atalanta on December 6, but not all supporters agree with the decision.

Lazio supporters have been boycotting their home matches since the beginning of the calendar year in protest of owner Claudio Lotito.

Fans are demanding that Lotito sell the club and had promised that they would not return to the stadium, aside from derby fixtures, until he had done so.

Despite home season tickets plummeting to around 3,000 season and away supporters regularly outnumbering home fans in the Stadio Olimpico in 2026-27, Lazio have surged to the top of the Serie A table and remain unbeaten after the first 12 league matches of the season.
